'''Frank Bryan Ntilikina''' {{IPA needed}} (born 28 July 1998) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[SIG Strasbourg]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = FRANK NTILINIKA INTERVIEW|url = http://www.givingbacksummeracademy.com/news/2015/9/2/frank-ntilinika-interview|website = Giving Back Globall Academy|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref> He grew up in the city of [[Strasbourg]]. Ntilikina stands 6 ft 5 in (196 cm) tall and is a [[point guard]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Frank Ntilikina profile SIG|url = http://sigstrasbourg.fr/player/frank-ntilikina/|website = SIGSTRASBOURG|access-date = 2016-08-22}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Ntilikina was born in [[Ixelles|Ixelles, Belgium]] on July 28, 1998 to [[Rwanda]]n parents.<ref name="draftexpress1">{{cite web|last1=Givony|first1=Jonathan|title=FIBA Europe U18 Championship Scouting Reports: Point Guards|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-Europe-U18-Championship-Scouting-Reports-Point-Guards-5197/|website=''DraftExpress.com''|accessdate=June 13, 2017|date=August 4, 2015}}</ref> At age three, he moved to [[Strasbourg|Strasbourg, France]].<ref name="nytimes">{{cite web|last1=Keh|first1=Andrew|title=Frank Ntilikina, a Top N.B.A. Prospect, Is Learning to Play With Fire|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/01/04/sports/basketball/frank-ntilikina-sig-strasbourg-france.html?_r=0|website=[[The New York Times]]|accessdate=June 13, 2017|date=January 4, 2017}}</ref> He began his club career at the age of five, playing for St-Joseph Strasbourg, before making the move to [[Strasbourg IG]]'s youth academy when he was 15.<ref>{{Cite web|title = F. Ntilikina: Deuxième parrain de Have A Basket !|url = http://haveabasket.com/2015/09/06/f-ntilikina-deuxieme-parrain-de-have-a-basket/|website = Have a Basket|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Ntilikina was invited to participate in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game in April 2014,<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://jordanbrandclassic.com/wp-content/uploads/archive/2014internationalgameboxscore.pdf|title = JBC International Game Official Basketball Box Score|date = 2014-04-18|access-date = 2016-02-05|website = |publisher = Jordan Brand Classic|last = |first = }}</ref> tallying six points, three rebounds and one assist in 23 minutes off the bench, and helped SIG to a French Youth League Championship title in the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Frank Ntilikina|url = http://sigstrasbourg.fr/player/frank-ntilikina/|website = SIGSTRASBOURG|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

In December 2015, Ntilikina signed a professional contract with SIG Strasbourg until June 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Frank Ntilikina signe un contrat de trois ans|url = http://sigstrasbourg.fr/2015/12/frank-ntilikina-signe-un-contrat-trois-ans/|website = SIGSTRASBOURG|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref> He had made his debut at the professional level even before the deal, seeing 15 minutes of action on April 4, 2015, in a French [[LNB Pro A]] [[2014–15 LNB Pro A season|2014–15 season]] contest against [[SOMB Boulogne-sur-Mer|Boulogne-sur-Mer]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Strasbourg / Boulogne-sur-Mer - 27ème journée - 2014/15 – Résultat match - Pro A – LNB.fr|url = http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200009/Resultat-match/8974/resultat-match|website = www.lnb.fr|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

Ntilikina dished out a game-high eight assists, to go along with 13 points and four rebounds, at the FIBA European Under-18 All-Star Game in September 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Red - Black {{!}} U18 All-Star Game (2015) {{!}} FIBA Europe|url = http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_byKWxHiNH4kgiRAG72AKU1.season_2015.roundID_11970.gameID_11970-1-A-1.html|website = www.fibaeurope.com|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

On October 15, 2015, Ntilikina logged his first [[EuroLeague]] minutes, scoring one point in 12:16 minutes of play against [[KK Crvena zvezda|KK Crvena Zvezda]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Crvena Zvezda Telekom Belgrade vs. Strasbourg - Game|url = http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=2&seasoncode=E2015#!boxscore|website = www.euroleague.net|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

In February 2016, he attended the "Basketball Without Borders Global Camp" in Toronto, Canada, during the [[NBA All-Star Weekend]].<ref>{{Cite web
| url = http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Basketball-Without-Borders-Global-Camp-Evaluations-Guards-and-Wings-5368/
| title = DraftExpress: Basketball Without Borders Global Camp Evaluations: Guards and Wings
| website = www.draftexpress.com
| access-date = 2016-02-28
}}</ref> He saw the court in 32 contests during the [[2015–16 Pro A season]], scoring 1.3 points per game, and he was named [[LNB Pro A Awards|the league's "Best Young Player"]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://basket-ballworld.fr/pro-a-frank-ntilikina-elu-meilleur-jeune-du-championnat/|title=Pro A : Frank Ntilikina élu meilleur jeune du championnat - Basket-BallWorld|date=2016-04-30|website=Basket-BallWorld|language=fr-FR|access-date=2016-05-03}}</ref>

In April 2017, Ntilikina entered his name into the [[2017 NBA Draft]]. By the end of the June 12 NBA Draft deadline, Ntilikina became only one of 10 international underclassmen to remain in the NBA Draft that year. Before that, though, he became one of 20 invites for the green room on draft night.

== International career ==
Ntilikina averaged 7.4 points, 2.0 assists, 1.6 boards, and one steal per game, en route to winning the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] with the Under-16 French Junior National Team.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Perfect France Beat Hosts, Lift Title  {{!}} U16 European Championship Men (2014){{!}} FIBA Europe|url = http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_YUjW-7-FJ,kK9s431Lyr41.season_2014.roundID_10124.coid_JQFDW0ZvGms5zlzSVTK7D3.articleMode_on.html|website = www.fibaeurope.com|access-date = 2016-02-05}}</ref>

He was spectacular in helping France's Under-18 national team win the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], scoring 31 points, including 7-for-10 from three-point range, in the championship game against the Under-18 Lithuanian team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/ls/#12368&12384-48-A|title=FIBA Live Statistics|website=www.fiba.com|access-date=2016-12-22}}</ref> He averaged 15.2 points, 4.5 assists, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.2 steals a game in the tournament, draining 50 percent of his field goal attempts, including 58.6 percent of his shots from long distance,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2016/France|title=France at the FIBA U18 European Championship Division A 2016 - FIBA.com|website=FIBA.com|access-date=2016-12-22}}</ref> en route to Most Valuable Player honors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/europe/u18/2016/news/france-take-home-title-after-thriller-with-lithuania|title=France take home the title after thriller with Lithuania|website=FIBA.com|access-date=2016-12-22}}</ref>
